question: What site-specific fish evidence does the SCSSAP Chapter 4 report for LPPWP and TMTP, and what source, taxonomy, methods, locality, and reuse gaps limit its use?

sourceAccess.accessMethod: Reviewed the project-hosted PDF using browser-extracted text on 2026-11-20. The source bibliography cites an undated Ancog et al. coastal biodiversity report. An exact-title/author and UPLB repository search was bounded and did not locate an independent copy; no access control was bypassed.
sections: Chapter 4 reference entry for Ancog et al. (20__ n.d.) and report title.
Annex 4.D combined LPPWP/TMTP summary, including the reported 56 fish species across both sites.
Annex 4.E Table 4.E.1: LPPWP fish portion and Figure 4.E.1 caption.
Annex 4.F Table 4.F.1: TMTP fish portion and Figure 4.F.1 caption.
sourceAccess.underlyingReportCitationAsPublished: Ancog, Rico C., R.M. Gamido, J. DeRamos, B. Samaniego, G.G. Villancio, J.R. Tabarno, D. Montesclaros Jr, J.F. Beloy, P.A. Felix, R. Sales Jr., M.B. Hernandez, and E. Austria. (20__ n.d.). Assessment of Biodiversity Associated with the Wetland Ecosystems of the Las Piñas-Parañaque Wetland Park (LPPWP) and the Tanza Marine Tree Park (TMTP): Coastal Biodiversity Report for LPPWP and TMTP. UPLB SESAM, DENR NCR, Adamson University.

LPPWP.figureContext: Figure 4.E.1 caption says fish sampling points, static traps, and sediment-coring points across lagoon and open-water habitats.
LPPWP.identityReview: Not performed in this batch. The printed strings include genus-only or apparent spelling forms, including “Sardinela sp.” and “Leignathus sp.”

TMTP.figureContext: Figure 4.F.1 caption says fish sampling and sediment-coring points in open water and mangrove forest.
TMTP.identityReview: Not performed in this batch. The printed strings include genus-only, numbered “sp.”, higher-rank, missing-epithet, and apparent spelling forms such as “Ambyglobius sp. 2/3,” “Hyporhampus sp.,” “Leignathus sp.,” “Gerres,” and “Pleuronectiformes sp.”

combinedClaim.interpretation: The combined report claim cannot be recalculated from the site rows without resolving generic labels, spelling variants, and possible cross-site identities. Do not infer the number of shared or unique taxa from the difference between these figures.

interpretation.evidenceType: Historical secondary summary of site-specific fish tables and per-hectare densities attributed to an undated report.
interpretation.sourceValue: The chapter identifies fish-table evidence for both wetland/coastal park contexts and reports a combined 56-fish-species total.
unresolved: Underlying study date, sampling design, field methods, sampling effort, specimen vouchers, exact station coordinates, and taxon-to-station assignments.
Source-faithful interpretation of non-binomial, numbered, missing-epithet, and spelling-variant strings.
Reconciliation of 20 and 52 printed site-table entries with the chapter’s combined count of 56 fish species.
Whether and how the derived table data may be redistributed or adapted.
interpretation.geographicScope: Park-level site context only. No channel, lagoon, shoreline, park, or protected-area geometry was created or validated.

limits: This is a project chapter reproducing a secondary table, not the underlying primary report or raw dataset.
A table label is not a taxonomic verification of an organism; no species assertion or occurrence row is added.
Per-hectare density values are historical source-reported values, not a current abundance estimate or fishing recommendation.
Park-level context is not an exact capture locality, and no record is assigned to surrounding Manila Bay, rivers, or other NCR waters.
No current access, legal status, fishing permission, safety, or fishability claim is made.
No figure, map, full list, or unlicensed source text is reproduced in the app or treated as cleared for public release.

decision.reason: The chapter exposes useful historical site-specific fish-table leads, but the underlying report is cited as undated and the exact taxa, survey methods/dates, locality resolution, combined counts, and reuse terms remain unresolved. Preserve it as research-only evidence and seek the cited source or a more traceable independent dataset before projection.

nextActions: Seek the underlying Ancog et al. Coastal Biodiversity Report through publicly indexed UPLB SESAM, DENR-NCR, Adamson University, and SCSSAP records; if located, verify survey dates, methods, table images, site names, sample stations, voucher basis, and reuse terms.

Run a separate source-faithful taxonomic crosswalk for every LPPWP/TMTP fish label; keep raw spellings and genus-level or higher-rank entries visible, and do not equate numbered “sp.” labels across tables without evidence.
Compare the source-reported site list with accession-level GBIF/OBIS evidence only after matching waterbody/site context and record-level date, identification, and reuse conditions.
Keep the NCR marine, brackish/wetland, and freshwater evidence lanes separate; NCR and Luzon remain incomplete.

sources.supports: SCSSAP Chapter 4, Annexes 4.D–4.F, the LPPWP and TMTP fish tables and sampling-map captions, and the chapter bibliography citation to the underlying undated Ancog et al. report.
SCSSAP project publication folder lists the Chapter 4 PDF in the Philippines TDA set.
